text: NVIDIA NIM packages optimized inference as microservices exposing an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, so existing OpenAI client code works against a self-hosted NIM unchanged.
A NIM is distributed as a prebuilt container from NGC; it auto-selects an optimized TensorRT-LLM engine for the detected GPU at startup.
Tensor parallelism splits each layer's weight matrices across GPUs; after the attention and MLP blocks an all-reduce sums the partial activations so every GPU holds the full result.
At small decode batch sizes tensor-parallel inference is communication-bound: each per-layer all-reduce moves only a few kilobytes and pays the fixed NCCL launch latency rather than bandwidth.
TensorRT-LLM compiles a model into an optimized engine with fused kernels, paged KV-cache and quantization; the engine is hardware-specific and built ahead of serving.
Triton Inference Server hosts TensorRT-LLM engines and provides in-flight (continuous) batching, dynamically adding and removing requests from the running batch to keep the GPU saturated.

On an NVSwitch system NCCL can use NVLS (NVLink SHARP), which performs the reduction inside the switch via multicast so each GPU sends its data once instead of the 2(N-1)/N passes a ring all-reduce needs.
An H100 SXM GPU has 18 fourth-generation NVLink links at about 26.5 GB/s each per direction, roughly 478 GB/s per-GPU unidirectional NVLink bandwidth.
FP8 weight quantization helps most in the memory-bandwidth-bound decode regime because halving the weight bytes cuts per-token weight traffic, lowering inter-token latency at low concurrency.
Paged KV-cache stores attention keys and values in fixed-size blocks like virtual memory pages, eliminating fragmentation and letting many sequences share GPU memory efficiently.

CUDA Graphs capture a sequence of GPU operations once and replay them as a single unit, removing per-kernel launch overhead; inference engines use this to hide the all-reduce launch latency during decode.
A reranker model rescores an initial set of retrieved passages by joint query-passage relevance, improving precision over pure vector similarity at the top of the list.
Hybrid retrieval fuses dense vector similarity with sparse keyword matching, so it catches both semantic paraphrases and exact term matches that either method alone would miss.
Groundedness checking validates that every claim in a generated answer is supported by the retrieved context; ungrounded answers are flagged or withheld to prevent hallucination.
The NeMo Agent Toolkit helps build, profile and evaluate multi-step agentic workflows, with hooks for tracing each tool call and step.
OpenTelemetry spans wrap each agent step (plan, retrieve, generate, validate) so latency and failures are attributable to a specific hop in production.
An embedding model maps text to a fixed-length vector so that semantically similar texts have nearby vectors under cosine similarity, forming the dense index for retrieval.
Speculative decoding uses a small draft model to propose several tokens that the large target model verifies in one pass, raising decode throughput when the draft is accurate.
Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions a single H100 into isolated instances with dedicated compute and memory, useful for serving several small models with guaranteed isolation.
Pipeline parallelism splits layers across GPUs into stages; the idle time while the pipeline fills and drains is called the bubble, reduced by micro-batching.
